title: A Reconstructional Origin of Universal Quantum Phase: Neutral-Parent Return, Saturation, and Born Read-Out
content: Quantum theory universally represents a physical history by a phase of the form exp(iS/ℏ), adds amplitudes across unresolved alternatives, and assigns probabilities through the Born rule. These structures are empirically successful but are ordinarily introduced only after a quantum state space has been assumed. This article develops a conditional reconstructional account of their common origin. The premetric reconstruction domain contains neither fields, action, amplitudes, nor quantum probabilities; a quantum platform arises only through constitutive read-out. On a connected platform whose persistent sectors descend from one neutral parent, Indefinite Reconstruction Stability requires locally readable primitive returns to agree on overlaps. Under compact connected scalar return, faithful overlap comparison, common orientation, and smooth-holonomy bridges, the local return data form one global U(1) phase structure. A continuous composition-preserving representation of additive post-read-out action then has the form Θ[γ]=exp(iS[γ]/a0). If the platform supplies one total action for joint histories and no additional action-calibration field, common-parent and overlap compatibility require the same a0 in every physical sector; empirical calibration identifies it with ℏ. The resulting invariant is an action period 2πℏ, not a minimum positive action. IRSP saturation retains every inequivalent admissible alternative, while an explicitly declared linear-composition bridge produces coherent history amplitudes. Positivity, normalization, orthogonal additivity, and a Hilbert-space event read-out then give the Born representation conditionally. The construction yields parameter-free falsification relations: equal action-to-phase slopes across sectors, one total-action phase for mixed-sector histories, invariance under observationally equivalent history refinements, and vanishing genuine third-order interference. A nonzero residual identifies which bridge fails. Previously reported constants, particle ratios, and law-selection results provide cross-sector motivation but are not premises. The construction does not derive Hilbert space or linear composition from IRSP alone; its bridges, inherited ingredients, and failure conditions are separately audited.
